## Landing note — a second, self-inflicted bug found and fixed on the way in (patch sets 1-3)

Worth recording because it is a nice demonstration of the difference between "the tests pass" and "the tests pass everywhere", and because the diagnosis was a second A/B experiment rather than a guess.

**Symptom.** Change 1512 patch sets 1 and 2 both took `Verified -1`. Every gate passed except a single matrix cell: `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)` reached 99% and then produced no further output until the 60-minute job timeout killed it, leaving orphaned `pytest`/`python` children. `py3.12`, `py3.13` and `macos-latest` all passed the identical tree in 12-20 minutes.

**First read was wrong.** I initially called it infrastructure and posted `recheck` — the 3-of-4-legs-pass pattern plus the orphan-process signature both point that way, and `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` (88 passed) and `tests/unit/test_review_bot_in_flight.py` (9 passed) ran clean on Python 3.11.13 locally. The recheck hung in exactly the same place, which killed the flake hypothesis: 3 for 3 is not a flake.

**What the local runs missed.** Reproducing the CI cell needs the *whole* CI command. Running the review-bot files alone passes; running the full suite on 3.11 passes too — until you add `--cov`. The trigger is py3.11 + coverage + xdist + the full suite.

**The A/B that settled attribution.** Identical command, identical interpreter, one variable:

| tree | result |
| --- | --- |
| clean `origin/main` @ 1afdbbd0be | 11184 passed, 26 skipped, **16m11s** |
| this change | **hangs at 99%** |

So the hang was mine, not the runner's.

**The mechanism.** `faulthandler` (`timeout -s ABRT`) dumped a worker holding a live `anyio` blocking portal — a `TestClient` — alongside a thread in `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:282 startup_sweep` -> `src/rebar/_snapshot/cache.py:133 entry_size`. My `/health` test had used `with TestClient(app)`, which runs the app **lifespan**: that starts the queue worker, the backfill reconciler and the snapshot janitor, and on exit awaits `queue.join()` under `shutdown_drain_seconds()` — a **1200-second** window. Every other lifespan-entering test in the suite stubs `reconcile_loop` (`_idle_reconcile_loop`, `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1462, :1490, :1631`); mine did not, so it started the real one plus a real filesystem sweep, and under coverage's tracing overhead that combination wedged the worker.

**The fix (patch set 3).** The test now awaits the `health()` handler directly instead of constructing an ASGI client. The route returns that dict as-is, so it IS the response body and the asserted contract is unchanged — but nothing background starts and no drain window is reachable. Verified: **11197 passed, 18 skipped, 13m33s** on py3.11 + coverage + xdist, no hang.

**Two things I would keep from this.** First, a test that enters a service's lifespan inherits every background task that service starts, including a 20-minute shutdown drain — asserting one JSON field never justifies that. Second, and more usefully: the same discipline that cracked the ticket's own bug cracked this one. Three legs passing looked like evidence of innocence; the controlled A/B on one variable was the thing that actually decided it.

Patch sets 1 and 2 each auto-queued an LLM review with **no manual nudge** (17m58s and ~6m respectively) — reported separately as the end-to-end observation this ticket asked for.
